description: Temporary compatibility contract for Azure Functions Core Tools. These six compiled records are the only Core Tools-required records in the current environment-migration surface. Their absence from other audited Core Tools call sites is not evidence that no other external consumer exists. The maintainer-approved policy permits removal of other migration APIs after host-internal zero and explicit compiled-baseline review.

audit.scope: Independent read-only audit of current Core Tools main plus separately audited historical vnext evidence.

branches.notes: Independent current audit found exactly three compile-time call sites, all passing SystemEnvironment.Instance. No direct IEnvironment member calls, no EnvironmentExtensions or ScriptSettingsManager use, and no reflection-based loading of these types.

Separately audited historical evidence at this exact tip found zero references. This entry does not claim that the independent current-main audit revalidated vnext or that vnext remains a supported current branch.

notPreserved.reason: The four IEnvironment members are not directly consumed by the audited Core Tools call sites and are not independently protected by this Core Tools contract. This does not prove absence of other external consumers. The maintainer-approved policy permits reviewed removal after host-internal zero, provided the six temporary Core Tools gates and their feature-owned removal requirements remain satisfied.

removalRequirements.replacement: Migrate Core Tools to the existing one-argument configuration-based FeatureFlags.IsEnabled path.
Add and ship a public configuration-only extension-bundle options parser, then migrate Core Tools.

Add and ship a public extension-bundle resolver or factory with narrow runtime options for local/Core Tools source URI, release channel, download and cache ownership, and non-App-Service flavor; migrate and release Core Tools bundle tests.
Remove the environment abstraction only after all three audited Core Tools call sites use their feature-owned replacements.
